LKT Akutkirurgi (Lærings- og KvalitetsTeam for Akut kirurgi) is a professional steering group under Danish Regions (Danske Regioner) responsible for driving quality improvement initiatives within acute surgery in Denmark [^src1]. The group plays a central role in the broader narrative of quality development in the Danish healthcare system, working alongside the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) to improve treatment standards through standardized indicators, risk adjustment, and continuous database management [^src3].

The initiative concluded its primary operational phase in 2022 [^src3]. Despite its conclusion, the impact of LKT Akutkirurgi continues to be reflected in national clinical databases, notably the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] [^src3]. The group's efforts are credited with driving improvements in patient survival rates over the preceding two years across all Danish regions [^src1]. Furthermore, LKT Akutkirurgi has directly contributed to the enhancement of specific clinical metrics. For instance, it worked on improving the documentation for the administration of antibiotics, which aligns with the goals of [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] [^src2]. It also contributed to a national increase in the percentage of patients receiving a CT scan within two hours, a metric tracked by [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] [^src2]. The development goals for both [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] and [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]]—which aim for at least 90% of patients to be scanned within 120 minutes—remain in direct alignment with the standards established by LKT Akutkirurgi [^src4].

Following the end of the LKT program in 2022, regional and local initiatives continue to be supported broadly, using the LKT's results and frameworks as an evidence-based reference point for ongoing quality development in acute abdominal surgery [^src3].
